study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: This study used pretrained normative models from the braincharts project (trained on 58,835 individuals aged 2-100 from 82 sites). For the current analysis, participants were recruited from the Oslo area as part of four studies: TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis study), STROKEMRI study, uTOP (Youth-TOP study), and sTOP (Forensic Psychiatry study). Data was acquired on two GE 3T scanners at Oslo University Hospital.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants (n = 782 male/608 female) were recruited from the Oslo area as part of four studies: the Thematically Organized Psychosis study (TOP) [30], the STROKEMRI study [31], The Youth-TOP study (uTOP) [32], and The Forensic Psychiatry study (sTOP) [33]." ... "We used pretrained normative models from https://github.com/predictiveclinical-neuroscience/braincharts. Briefly, models were trained using data of 58835 individuals aged 2-100 from 82 sites."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Haukvik2025.pdf.md: Methods / Participants, L33; Methods / Normative models, L57

answer.TOP: Source of participants for clinical groups (SSD-NV) and healthy controls; recruitment from hospital wards, out-patient clinics, and Norwegian national population registry

answer.STROKEMRI: Source of healthy control participants; recruitment by newspaper ads and word of mouth

answer.uTOP: Source of younger participants (12-18 years); recruitment from Norwegian national population registry

answer.sTOP: Source of forensic psychiatry participants (SSD-V and nonSSD-V); recruitment from high security hospital wards and prisons

answer.Pre-trained braincharts model: Normative model training (58,835 individuals from 82 sites); used for computing deviation scores

answer.Calibration set (HC n=998): Model calibration/fine-tuning to adjust the pretrained model to local scanner data (site adaptation)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The pretrained normative models were applied to local data. A calibration set of 998 healthy controls was used to fine-tune model parameters to account for scanner differences. The remaining participants (n=392 males) were divided into four groups for analysis: SSD-V (n=38), nonSSD-V (n=20), SSD-NV (n=138), and HC (n=196).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "998 healthy controls (390 male/608 female) were used as a calibration set to adjust the model to our data [20]." ... "To account for the absence of scanner data used to acquire data in the model, an additional harmonization step was implemented. An unmatched group of healthy controls (n = 998) was utilized to fine-tune model parameters, enabling the application of normative models to unseen sites."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study used pretrained normative models from the braincharts project. The models were trained on 58,835 individuals aged 2-100 from 82 sites. The train/test split for the original model training is not reported in this paper. For site adaptation, 998 healthy controls were used as a calibration set to fine-tune model parameters to local scanner data.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The pretrained braincharts normative model was trained on data from individuals aged 2-100 years. Detailed age statistics (mean, SD, median, IQR) for the original training cohort are not reported in this paper. The current study's local sample (calibration set + analysis groups) age statistics are provided in Table 1, but these are not the normative model training data.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Briefly, models were trained using data of 58835 individuals aged 2-100 from 82 sites."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution for the pretrained braincharts normative model (58,835 individuals) is not reported in this paper. The paper references Rutherford et al. (2022) for details on the normative models. The current study's analysis sample was all male (n=392) due to scarcity of eligible women in forensic psychiatry populations.
